answer: That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the ember embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Since the ocean index is rebuilt each epoch, the sparrow audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 83% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. That is 34 dollars per alias. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
